tags.name: mcp-oauth
tags.description: The public legs of MCP OAuth authorization. POST /v1/mcp-connections/{id}/connect returns an authorizationUrl to open in the user's browser; GET /v1/mcp/oauth/authorize sets a transaction cookie and redirects to the provider; after the user consents, the provider redirects to GET /v1/mcp/oauth/callback, which stores the credential and redirects to the dashboard; the caller then polls GET /v1/mcp-connections/{id} until status is connected. client-metadata is fetched by the provider itself during dynamic client registration.

ApiKey.description: Tenant API key minted by POST /v1/apikeys; sent as `Authorization: Bearer ba_…`. Covers the tenant integration surface.

DashboardJwt.description: Supabase-issued dashboard session; only the Blazing Agents dashboard holds one

get.summary: Serve the OAuth client metadata document
get.description: The client metadata document (CIMD) an MCP authorization server fetches during dynamic client registration; its `redirect_uris` binds this deployment's callback URL. Public; no credential required.

get.summary: Begin the MCP OAuth authorization redirect
get.description: Consumes a one-time `setup` launch token, binds a short-lived HttpOnly cookie to the transaction, and 302-redirects the browser to the MCP authorization server's consent page. Public; no credential required.

302.description: Redirect to the provider's authorization page; sets the `blazing_mcp_oauth` transaction cookie

post.description: Exchanges a setup token for a one-time launch URL that hands the Connection's OAuth approval to the bound Tenant admin's browser. Only a dashboard JWT may call this.

get.description: The provider's redirect target after user consent. Validates the transaction cookie and `state`, stores the issued credential on the Connection, clears the cookie, and 302-redirects to the dashboard with a safe `mcpOAuth` status only — provider parameters never reach the dashboard URL. Public; no credential required.

302.description: Redirect to the dashboard with `?mcpOAuth=success&id=…` or `?mcpOAuth=error`; clears the `blazing_mcp_oauth` cookie

post.description: Verifies a Supabase dashboard JWT directly (it runs before any Tenant exists, ahead of the Tenant-auth and subscription middleware) and provisions the Tenant, admin Agent and admin Workspace on first call; later calls return the existing Tenant. Only a dashboard JWT may call this.

get.description: JWT-only. Returns the tenant record. An API-key-authenticated request is rejected here with generic 401 `unauthorized`: the credential type is insufficient for this resource.
Returns the static plan catalog. Only a dashboard JWT may call this.

post.description: Creates a hosted checkout attempt for the tenant and returns its URL. Only a dashboard JWT may call this.

200.description: The checkout attempt and hosted URL

post.description: Re-checks a checkout attempt against the billing provider and reconciles the tenant's subscription state. Only a dashboard JWT may call this.

409.description: Checkout evidence does not match the tenant

post.description: Mints a `ba_` token, returns it once. Max 5 per tenant (enforced in `ApiKeyService.create`). Only a dashboard JWT may call this route.

201.description: The created API key and its one-time token

get.description: List only (no get-by-id); wire-shape rows with the 2-char display fragment, no digest. Only a dashboard JWT may call this.

delete.description: Hard delete; dead on the next request. The `id` route param is validated at the HTTP boundary. Only a dashboard JWT may call this.

Marks the tenant deleting: new executions block immediately and queued Task runs are cancelled; work already running finishes. Permanent deletion is scheduled 24 hours out on the durable `tenantDeletion` workflow and can be cancelled until then. The response reports the scheduled deletion. Only a dashboard JWT may call this route.

get.description: The tenant's self-set quota row per ticket 09, plus the deletion lifecycle state (`deletion: null` until `DELETE /v1/tenant` runs). `quota: null` means unlimited (no row). Any valid credential (API key or dashboard JWT) may call this.

patch.description: Upserts (or clears, on `quota: null`) the tenant's self-set quota row per ticket 09. `monetizationEnabled` flips the tenant-wide merchant billing switch — disabling discards every merchant usage event the provider has not accepted. Any valid credential (API key or dashboard JWT) may call this. `quota: undefined` (key omitted) leaves the existing quota untouched; `quota: null` deletes the row — pass `quota` through untouched so a name-only rename does not wipe the tenant's limits.

post.description: Cancels a deletion scheduled by `DELETE /v1/tenant` while its 24-hour window is still open. Runs queued for cancellation stay cancelled; the scheduled cleanup workflow never runs. Returns `tenant_not_deleting` when nothing is scheduled and `tenant_deletion_in_progress` once the deadline has passed. Only a dashboard JWT may call this route.

Verifies the supplied platform credentials against the live chat API, derives the installation identity from the token, generates the Telegram webhook secret, and returns the computed callback `webhookUrl`. An enabled Telegram Connection is then registered with Telegram (`drop_pending_updates: true`); when registration fails the Connection is still created but persisted disabled with a failing `webhook_url` health check. The target Agent must exist in the tenant. Any valid credential may call this.

get.description: All of the tenant's Chat Connections, `createdAt` then `id` ascending. Any valid credential may call this.
Cursored list of the Connection's durable outbound deliveries, `createdAt` then `id` descending. Any valid credential may call this.

post.description: Re-sends a delivery whose sender stopped before the outcome was recorded. The body is a sworn statement: `expectedAttempt` must match the recorded attempt and both flags must be `true`, acknowledging the platform may already hold the message. The Connection must be enabled. Any valid credential may call this.

get.description: One Chat Connection by ID. Out-of-tenant IDs 404. Any valid credential may call this.

patch.description: Updates the Connection's name or optional configuration fields; at least one field is required. `webhookUrl` is read-only and computed from the API origin. Changing `businessMode` on an enabled Telegram Connection re-registers the webhook with the matching update set and `drop_pending_updates: false` (registration failure → 502 `chat_webhook_registration_failed`, after the configuration was saved). Out-of-tenant updates 404. Any valid credential may call this.

409.description: The Telegram bot already delivers to a webhook outside this deployment

502.description: Telegram webhook registration failed after the update was saved

delete.description: Deletes the Connection and its stored credentials. For Telegram, BA first deregisters the bot webhook best-effort; a deregistration failure is logged and never blocks the delete. Out-of-tenant deletes 404. Any valid credential may call this.

post.description: Replaces the Connection's platform credentials. Telegram supplies only the bot token and BA generates a fresh webhook secret; on an enabled Connection BA then re-registers the webhook with the new secret and `drop_pending_updates: false` (registration failure → 502 `chat_webhook_registration_failed`, after the credentials were already saved). The new credentials must verify against the live chat API and identify the same installation; pending deliveries pinned to the previous credential version become repairable. Any valid credential may call this.

200.description: The chat connection with rotated credentials

409.description: The Telegram bot already delivers to a webhook outside this deployment

502.description: Telegram webhook registration failed after the credentials were saved

post.description: Re-verifies the stored credentials against the live chat API, persists the fresh health evidence, and returns the updated Connection. Any valid credential may call this.

200.description: The chat connection with refreshed health

post.description: Disables the Connection and returns the updated record. Disabled Connections acknowledge verified inbound webhooks with 200 and drop them, and reject delivery repair. BA does not contact the chat platform, so a registered Telegram webhook stays registered until the next enable or delete. Any valid credential may call this.

Enables the Connection and returns the updated record. For Telegram, BA registers the computed `webhookUrl` with the bot's stored webhook secret and drops pending updates. A webhook already registered outside this deployment → 409 `chat_webhook_conflict`; a registration failure → 502 `chat_webhook_registration_failed` and the Connection stays disabled. Any valid credential may call this.

409.description: The Telegram bot already delivers to a webhook outside this deployment

post.description: Creates a provider. The API key goes to Vault (encrypted); the providers row holds only the vault pointer + the last-4 display fragment. Unique per (tenant, name); max 20 per tenant. The key is write-only + immutable (PATCH mutates the name only). Any valid credential (API key or dashboard JWT) may call this.

409.description: Provider name already exists

get.description: List only (no pagination; bounded by the 20-per-tenant cap). Each item contains id, name, providerType, createdAt, and updatedAt. Any valid credential (API key or dashboard JWT) may call this.
Discovers the catalog of model ids the provider exposes for the tenant's credential.
Discovers the thinking levels supported by the given model on this provider. `known` is false when the provider does not advertise the model's capabilities.

Returns the provider record. Out-of-tenant reads 404 (no existence leakage). The key is write-only; the response carries only the last-4 display fragment. Any valid credential (API key or dashboard JWT) may call this.

patch.description: Mutates only the display name. The endpoint, key, and `providerType` are immutable (the key is create-or-delete only — rotate by create-new → repoint agents → delete-old). Out-of-tenant updates 404. Any valid credential (API key or dashboard JWT) may call this.

409.description: Provider name already exists

delete.description: Deletes the provider and its Vault secret in one transaction. Returns 409 `provider_in_use` with referencing Agent IDs while any Agent still uses the provider. Provider removal never reconfigures referencing Agents implicitly. Out-of-tenant deletes return 404. Any valid credential (API key or dashboard JWT) may call this.

409.description: Provider is still in use by agents

post.description: Creates a workspace. Any valid credential (API key or dashboard JWT) may call this.

get.description: Cursored list of the tenant's workspaces. Any valid credential (API key or dashboard JWT) may call this.
Returns the workspace record. Out-of-tenant reads 404 (no existence leakage). Any valid credential (API key or dashboard JWT) may call this.

put.description: Updates the workspace. Out-of-tenant updates 404. Any valid credential (API key or dashboard JWT) may call this.

delete.description: Enqueues workspace deletion. Returns 202 while the deletion workflow runs and 204 when it completed synchronously; 404 out-of-tenant, 409 `workspace_in_use` while agents reference it and 409 `workspace_busy` while it is busy. Any valid credential (API key or dashboard JWT) may call this.

409.description: Workspace is in use or busy

post.description: Creates a Connection to a remote MCP server and validates it. The unique (tenantId, name) constraint maps to 409 `mcp_connection_name_conflict`. Any valid credential (API key or dashboard JWT) may call this.

409.description: Connection name already exists

get.description: Lists the tenant's Connections.

post.summary: Start OAuth connect for a connection
post.description: Starts the OAuth authorization-code connect flow for the Connection and returns the upstream authorization URL. Only a dashboard JWT may call this.
Probes the Connection's MCP server with its stored credentials and returns the live result. Out-of-tenant reads 404.
Replaces the Connection's endpoint and credentials and revalidates it. Returns `connected` or `needs_auth`. Out-of-tenant updates 404.

get.description: Returns the Connection record. Out-of-tenant reads 404 (no existence leakage).

patch.description: Renames the Connection. The unique (tenantId, name) constraint maps to 409 `mcp_connection_name_conflict`. Out-of-tenant updates 404.

409.description: Connection name already exists

delete.description: Deletes the Connection and revokes stored credentials. A Connection still attached to an Agent returns 409 `mcp_connection_in_use`. Out-of-tenant deletes 404.

409.description: Connection still attached to an agent

Runs one turn of the agent without saving a session and streams the answer as plain text. Send exactly one of `prompt` or `promptId`; `variables` is allowed only with `promptId`. With object output, the stream is JSON text that matches your schema. A failure before the stream starts returns a JSON error. Once the stream has started, a failure ends it early and the status stays 200.

example.prompt: Explain how to reset a password in one sentence.

prompt.description: The prompt to answer. Send either `prompt` or `promptId`.

promptId.description: ID of a saved prompt to use instead of `prompt`.

variables.description: Values for the saved prompt's variables. Allowed only with `promptId`, and must name exactly the prompt's variables.

output.description: What to stream back: `{"type":"text"}` for text, or `{"type":"object","schema":{…}}` for JSON that matches a JSON Schema.

version.description: Agent version to run. Leave it out to run the current version.

userId.description: Your end user's ID, used for usage attribution.

metadata.description: Your own key-value data, recorded with the usage.

get.description: Cursored list of the tenant's sessions for an agent, ordered `updatedAt` desc. Items carry `messageCount` + `lastMessagePreview` (maintained by the commit RPC). The list is scoped by `tenantId` so an unknown/foreign `agentId` simply yields an empty page (no existence leakage). Any valid credential (API key or dashboard JWT) may call this.

post.summary: Create a session and run the first turn
post.description: Mints an `ss_` session id, returns `201` + `Location`, materializes the Session after request/quota validation, then runs the first Turn. The response streams the UI message protocol over SSE.

201.description: Server-sent events; each event's data is one TurnStreamChunk (AI SDK UI message stream protocol)

schema.description: URL of the created session resource

Location.description: URL of the created session resource

get.description: Globally latest nonempty Sessions by default, or one latest Session per Agent with `byAgent=true`. Both modes support the same optional Attribution filter and `(updatedAt, id)` keyset cursor.

Transcript as `UIMessage[]` verbatim, paginated backwards (newest page first, chronological inside every page) with a mutually-exclusive `?after` forward cursor (the poll loop). Default `limit` 50, max 200. Out-of-tenant and soft-deleted sessions 404 (no existence leakage). Any valid credential (API key or dashboard JWT) may call this.

delete.description: Soft-deletes the session (sets `deletedAt`); the id thereafter 404s everywhere. `deleteArtifacts=true` also deletes the session's Artifacts. Out-of-tenant and already-deleted sessions 404 (no existence leakage). Any valid credential (API key or dashboard JWT) may call this.

post.summary: Resume a session with the next turn
post.description: Runs the next Turn on an existing session — `404` on unknown or soft-deleted id (strict, no silent create). `trigger: "regenerate-message"` truncate-and-rerun rides on this route only. The response streams the UI message protocol over SSE.

200.description: Server-sent events; each event's data is one TurnStreamChunk (AI SDK UI message stream protocol)

409.description: Approval already decided or session busy

409.description: Tool approvals are still awaiting decisions

schema.description: URL of the created memory resource

Cap: 100 prompts/tenant → 400 `prompt_limit_reached`. Any valid credential (API key or dashboard JWT) may call this.

409.description: Prompt name already exists

get.description: Lists the tenant's prompts, ordered by updatedAt desc. Not paginated (only sessions + transcripts are paginated in MVP per the contract); bounded by the 100/tenant cap. `variables` is derived on each read. `userId` filters by end-user attribution (ADR-0001): absent = no filter, `''` = tenant-level prompts only. Any valid credential (API key or dashboard JWT) may call this.
Returns the prompt record with `variables` derived from the template. Out-of-tenant reads 404 (no existence leakage). Any valid credential (API key or dashboard JWT) may call this.

patch.description: Updates name and/or template. Mutable, latest-wins, no versioning. `variables` is re-derived on read. The unique (tenantId, name) constraint maps to 409 `prompt_name_conflict`. Out-of-tenant updates 404. Any valid credential (API key or dashboard JWT) may call this.

409.description: Prompt name already exists

delete.description: Hard-deletes the prompt. Delete never blocks: nothing references a prompt (invocation resolves at request time and persists only rendered text), so a deleted `promptId` simply 404s on the next invocation. Out-of-tenant deletes 404. Any valid credential (API key or dashboard JWT) may call this.

get.description: Returns the tenant's current merchant connection, or null when none exists. The credential is write-only; the response carries only the display fragment. Any valid credential (API key or dashboard JWT) may call this.

200.description: The current merchant connection, or null

post.description: Verifies the credential against the provider, then creates the connection atomically: the previous non-retired connection is retired and the credential goes to Vault. Any valid credential (API key or dashboard JWT) may call this.

patch.description: Mutates status (active/disconnected), guard configuration, or rotates the credential. Rotation re-verifies the credential and requires the same merchant account. Any valid credential (API key or dashboard JWT) may call this.

409.description: Merchant account mismatch

delete.description: Retires the current connection. The Vault secret is retained so already-recorded usage events keep delivering. Any valid credential (API key or dashboard JWT) may call this.

get.description: Keyset-paginated bindings on the tenant's current merchant connection, ordered by userId. Any valid credential (API key or dashboard JWT) may call this.

put.summary: Bind a user to a merchant customer
put.description: Validates the customer id against the provider, then upserts the binding on the tenant's current merchant connection. Any valid credential (API key or dashboard JWT) may call this.

delete.description: Removes the binding on the tenant's current merchant connection. Any valid credential (API key or dashboard JWT) may call this.

get.description: Keyset-paginated merchant usage events, newest first. `workflowIssue` surfaces a terminal DBOS delivery attempt; `nextAction` names the operator step. Any valid credential (API key or dashboard JWT) may call this.

Delivery-health aggregate: all-time counts per event status, the last acceptance and oldest pending timestamps, and a UTC daily window of accepted events/tokens versus pending events so operators can see at a glance whether merchant delivery is flowing. Any valid credential (API key or dashboard JWT) may call this.
Returns the immutable merchant usage event with its delivery status and workflow projection. Out-of-tenant reads 404. Any valid credential (API key or dashboard JWT) may call this.

post.description: Re-arms a failed, uncertain, or terminally-stuck pending event as a new DBOS workflow execution with the same frozen payload. Any valid credential (API key or dashboard JWT) may call this.

409.description: Event state does not allow this action

post.summary: Release an unmapped merchant usage event
post.description: Rebinds an unmapped event to its current customer binding, rebuilds the provider payload, and enqueues delivery. Requires the binding to still map the event's user. Any valid credential (API key or dashboard JWT) may call this.

409.description: Event state conflict or missing customer binding

post.description: Discards a non-deliverable event (unmapped, incomplete, failed, uncertain, or expired). The frozen payload is retained. Any valid credential (API key or dashboard JWT) may call this.

409.description: Event state does not allow this action

get.description: The tenant's own usage over the daily-rollup table. `?from=&to=&agentId=&sessionId=&groupBy=&limit=` per ticket 12. Range capped at 31 days (default last 30 days ending today UTC). `groupBy=session` is top-N by tokens (default 50, max 200); the others are exhaustive and bounded. Response `{ buckets, totals }`, no pagination. Any valid credential (API key or dashboard JWT) may call this.
Aggregate usage overview for the tenant. Any valid credential (API key or dashboard JWT) may call this.

Same shape as `GET /v1/usage` but scoped to one agent (the per-agent conditional keep from ticket 09, satisfied as a PK prefix scan). The `agentId` path param is the authoritative scope; an explicit `?agentId=` on the query string is ignored. Any valid credential (API key or dashboard JWT) may call this.

200.description: Usage buckets and totals for the agent

post.description: Creates a task. Scheduled tasks submit their product generation to DBOS after insert. `submit: true` enqueues a run immediately (on-demand's only trigger alongside creation) with a server-minted random run id. This path is NOT idempotent — each call creates a new task + new run. For run-level idempotency, use `POST /v1/tasks/{taskId}/runs` with an idempotency key. Returns `{ task, runId }` — `runId` is null unless `submit` is true. Any valid credential (API key or dashboard JWT) may call this.

202.description: The created task with its queued run id

get.description: Cursored list of the tenant's tasks, `updatedAt` desc. `?agentId=` filters by agent. Items embed a compact `latestRun` `{ id, status, finishedAt }` (join on `latestRunId`) to kill N+1 status polling. Soft-deleted tasks are excluded. Any valid credential may call.
Returns the task record. Out-of-tenant and soft-deleted tasks 404 (no existence leakage). Any valid credential may call this.

patch.description: Updates name/prompt/schedule/enabled. `agentId` is immutable (repoint = recreate). Schedule/enabled changes submit the new product generation to DBOS. Out-of-tenant and soft-deleted tasks 404. Any valid credential may call this.

delete.description: Soft delete (`deletedAt`); the id 404s everywhere thereafter and schedule synchronization removes DBOS state. Returns `400` while a run is active (it must complete or be canceled first). Runs and their sessions are kept; purge policy joins the Retention fog. Any valid credential may call this.

post.description: Run-now for any task (on-demand's only trigger; also tests a cron). `202` + `{ runId }` queued run; `409` if one is already active. Optional client idempotency key: when present, hashed with `tenantId` + `taskId` to a deterministic run id — a replay returns the existing run instead of enqueuing a new one. Any valid credential may call this.

409.description: A run is already active for the task

get.description: Cursored list of a task's runs, newest first (`createdAt` desc). Missing and out-of-tenant tasks return the same non-enumerating 404 as the other Task operations.
Returns the run record `{ id, status, error, sessionId, startedAt, finishedAt, ... }`. Out-of-tenant runs 404 (no existence leakage). Any valid credential may call this.

get.summary: List a task run's session messages
get.description: The task-run session transcript as `UIMessage[]` verbatim, paginated backwards (newest page first, chronological inside every page) with a mutually-exclusive `?after` forward cursor (the poll loop). Same shape as `GET /v1/agents/{agentId}/sessions/{sessionId}/messages` — the task run resolves to its server-minted session, and the session's messages are returned. The Session response is extended with the run's `status`, `error`, and `finishedAt`, allowing one polling request to observe messages and run completion. Runs without a session (not yet started) return an empty page. Out-of-tenant runs 404 (no existence leakage). Any valid credential may call this.

200.description: A page of session messages plus run state

post.description: Cooperative cancel. Sets `cancelRequestedAt` (the workflow's 250ms cancellation poll aborts via AbortController). Any valid credential may call this. Task ownership is checked first, so missing and foreign tasks receive the same non-enumerating 404. For an owned task, cancellation remains idempotent: a missing, mismatched, inactive, or terminal run is a no-op 204.

Inbound Polar webhook. The Standard Webhooks signature headers (`webhook-id`, `webhook-signature`, `webhook-timestamp`) are verified against the endpoint secret before the event is stored and reconciled; the body is the Polar event envelope. Duplicate deliveries are acknowledged idempotently. Public; the signature is the credential.

202.description: The event was accepted or already seen

post.description: Inbound webhook target for Slack and Telegram. The platform signature (Slack `x-slack-signature` with `x-slack-request-timestamp`; Telegram `x-telegram-bot-api-secret-token`) is verified against the Connection's stored credentials before any event is dispatched; the body is the platform's native event envelope (Slack may send it form-encoded under `payload`). Disabled Connections answer signed Slack URL verification, then acknowledge and drop other verified events with 200. Public; the signature is the credential.

200.description: The adapter's response — Slack URL verification echoes its `challenge`; event deliveries are acknowledged
